_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.rom:9D8D: CONFIRMED shape: ChallengeCountdown (ram_00BD) is a per-tick countdown timer, gated by ram_1DFB being zero (an unidentified pause/animation-lock condition) and decremented once per pass through this routine. Set to $80 (128) at two points: game boot (rom:sub_B13E) and inside rom:sub_9DAF (the same area that increments the earlier-rejected-then-corrected ram_0042/0043 pair, see rom:9DBE) -- so it restarts roughly once per some game-level event, not once per frame from boot to end. When it reaches exactly $60 (i.e. 32 ticks after being armed at $80), rom:D021's gated check (via ram_0061) becomes reachable -- this is the actual trigger window for entering ChallengeHitCount's challenge-stage tracking, not ram_0061 alone. When the countdown instead reaches 0 (BEQ path, the timer running all the way out without the challenge condition firing), ChallengeHitCountBin/ram_0059/ram_004B all reset to 0 -- reads as a timeout/cleanup path distinct from a successful challenge-stage entry.
comments.rom:9D0F: CONFIRMED: a state-reset routine setting several bytes to 1, including ram_0046 (the byte rom:sub_970B's formation-pattern-selection code compares against 13/25/37/49/61). REVISES the earlier read of ram_0046 as a wave-number candidate: this routine is called from exactly two places -- game boot (rom:sub_B13E, alongside a full zero-page clear) and rom:9DA5 (inside the same countdown-timer area as rom:9D8D) -- neither of which fires once per wave on its own. Live data (existing tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua capture) shows ram_0046 cycling repeatedly through roughly 1-62 many dozens of times across a single ~10-minute recording, far more often than a per-wave reset would allow -- so something ELSE (not yet found) also increments/resets it, and it reads as a per-formation-entry-step sub-counter within a wave, not the wave number itself. The 13/25/37/49/61 boundary values are a real, evenly-spaced-by-12 sequence worth understanding on their own terms, just not as wave-number checkpoints.
comments.rom:B406: CONFIRMED LIVE, screenshot-verified: found by grepping for the digit-extraction idiom (AND #$0F / four LSRs) instead of guessing, the same method that found ram_0043's earlier (unrelated) digit-render use. This is the REAL on-screen score display, at a completely different location than the ram_2724-family accumulator this project spent a previous pass tracing: ScoreDigit0-ScoreDigit4 ($275F-$2763), five bytes holding one decimal digit (0-9) each, most-significant digit first. Confirmed two ways: (1) captured a screenshot plus a full RAM dump at the same exact frame, twice, at two different points in run-01.inp (scores 28200 and 32250 visibly on screen), and both times the five digit bytes matched the visible digits exactly, byte for byte; (2) traced the same five bytes across the entire recording and the implied score climbs smoothly with no discontinuities, unlike the earlier candidate. Value 0x0A (ten) appears to serve as a leading-zero-suppression/blank marker in the wider rendering code (rom:sub_B3B4's own array uses the same sentinel) -- not confirmed for this specific 5-byte array, but consistent with the shape. CORRECTED (see docs/pitfalls.md): several passes traced 'the whole of run-01.inp' and reported a peak score around 32,000 -- that was only ever the first ~35900 of the file's real 104454 frames, because this project's own probe scripts had been calling MACHINE:exit() based on a wrong belief about where the recording ended (a MAME 'Total playback frames' summary line was mistaken for the file's true length, when it actually just reports wherever the *process* stopped). Rerun with a properly generous exit threshold: the score climbs past 250,000 by frame 102000 and the recording's true end (confirmed via the same rerun) is frame 104454, at which point playback exhausts and the game freezes on a static state (almost certainly the last life being lost). This is the wave-36/200,000+ run the user described all along -- it was in this file the entire time.
comments.rom:D021: CONFIRMED shape (SED/BCD arithmetic), CANDIDATE match for the user's challenge-stage hint: gated by ram_0061 being nonzero, increments ChallengeHitCount (ram_008A) by 1 in BCD each time this runs, and unconditionally increments ChallengeHitCountBin (ram_0063, a plain binary counter -- likely a parallel encoding of the same event, matching the pattern already seen at rom:9DBE for a different pair of adjacent bytes). LIVE-CHECKED against run-01.inp, twice: first with tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua's coarse 60-frame sampling (found ChallengeHitCount sitting at 0 for ~29000 of ~35900 frames, then a burst of raw byte values up to 51 over ~1500 frames, then a reset to 0), then re-checked with a narrow unthrottled tap (tools/probe-challenge-writes.lua) that caught every single write: exactly 33 BCD increments before the reset, i.e. the counter genuinely ran 1,2,3...,9,10,11,...,19,20,...,29,30,31,32,33 -- CORRECTING an earlier misreading of the raw byte 0x33 (51 in plain decimal) as the count itself rather than decoding it as BCD digits '3' and '3'. 33 out of the manual's 40-ships-per-stage figure lines up closely with the user's own account of NOT getting a perfect challenge clear -- likely is a near-1:1 kill count after all, not a points-in-some-unit value as first guessed. Also confirmed live: this fires from PC $D02B every single time, exclusively, and each firing coincides exactly (same frame) with a real write into the score-shaped accumulator at rom:93E0 -- see that comment for what that accumulator's value implies and why it isn't fully settled either. ram_0061 itself (the gate) is heavily referenced elsewhere ($966E-$9E03). MAPPED since this comment was written: see rom:9DD8 for what sets and clears it (a Wave mod 4 == 2 schedule -- this is what determines a given wave is a challenge wave, an item that was flagged open in docs/FINDINGS.md for a full pass) and rom:D097 for the group-of-8 scoring gate (ChallengeValueCycle, ram_005A) that directly explains the user's wave-36 point-value hint.
comments.rom:9DBE: CONFIRMED LIVE as the wave counter, correcting a wrong rejection earlier in this same file. Increments ram_0043 (WaveBCD) by 1 in BCD, alongside a plain (non-BCD) INC of ram_0042 (Wave) -- two parallel encodings (binary + BCD-display) of the same counter. RETRACTED: an earlier pass said this pair 'only ever reached 5' in run-01.inp and rejected it as wave number -- that check was against data truncated to the first ~35900 of the recording's true 104454 frames (a bug in this project's own probe scripts, which had been calling MACHINE:exit() based on a wrong assumption about the file's length -- see docs/pitfalls.md and docs/FINDINGS.md for the full story). Rerun with the correct frame range: ram_0042 (raw binary) and ram_0043 (properly BCD-decoded, i.e. high-nibble*10+low-nibble, NOT its raw byte value) agree with each other exactly at every checkpoint from frame 6000 through 102000, and both track the on-screen score (rom:ScoreDigit0-4) precisely the way a wave counter should: value 16 at a score around 111,520 and value 28 at a score around 201,980, matching the user's own recollection (~wave 17 at ~111K, exactly wave 28 at ~200K) closely enough to call this settled. On BCD overflow (carry, i.e. wave 100), resets both back to 1 (not 0) and clears four other bytes (ram_0058/005A/0049/005B) -- reads as 'a new wave is starting' bookkeeping, now confirmed rather than just shape-matched.
comments.rom:93E0: CONFIRMED shape (SED/BCD arithmetic) AND NOW LIVE-CONFIRMED ACTIVE, correcting an earlier retraction in this same file: a 3-byte BCD accumulator add (Y=2..0, adding ram_006C,Y into ram_2724,Y) with carry chaining into a further BCD digit pair (ram_2762/ram_2763, capped at 10 via CMP #$0A/SBC #$0A). A second, identical block immediately after (rom:9412) does the same into ram_2727,Y instead, selected by whether X is zero. RETRACTED: an earlier pass here said none of ram_2724-2729 changed across a whole recording, checked only against a 60-frame-interval snapshot, and concluded the routine was probably inactive -- wrong. A narrow, unthrottled, frame-exact write-tap (tools/probe-challenge-writes.lua, frames 28800-31800 of run-01.inp) shows rom:93E8 (the STA inside this loop) firing on every single frame without exception, most often adding zero (a no-op pass) but with real, substantial BCD increments landing exactly in step with rom:D021's ChallengeHitCount events. The 60-frame sampling simply never happened to land on a frame where the accumulated value had moved net-net, which is not the same as the code not running -- see the toolkit's own pitfall on exactly this failure mode. BYTE ORDER, worked out from the loop's own Y=2-down-to-0 addition order (lowest digits added first, so carry propagates into the higher ones next): ram_2726 is the LOWEST BCD digit pair (confirmed live: cycles through the full 00-99 range repeatedly within the captured window), ram_2725 is the next pair up (climbed 16->34 across the same window), ram_2724 is the HIGHEST pair captured here (stayed at 00 throughout) -- opposite of the address order guessed at first. RETRACTED, twice over, both times by the same truncated-data bug (the MAME playback-frame-count pitfall documented at rom:9DBE): the ram_2724-2726/ram_2727-2729 labels ScoreHi/Mid/Lo were first removed on the grounds that 'the score never climbs past roughly 111,000 in this recording' -- which was true only of the truncated first third of run-01.inp, exactly the same bug that caused the wave-number rejection at rom:9DBE. RESTORED, corrected, and independently verified after consulting the private reference source (see docs/FINDINGS.md's cross-check section): the reference names the equivalent structure P1BONUS/P2BONUS and describes it as an extra-life bonus accumulator, separate from the score -- that specific identity was tested directly against this ROM's own bytes rather than taken on trust, and it does NOT hold here. A live write-tap on ram_2724 (the highest-order byte, changing only when the packed value crosses a 10,000-unit boundary) against the full, correctly-lengthed run-01.inp caught two crossings; both times, a screenshot at that exact frame showed the on-screen score reading EXACTLY 10x the packed value (10018 -> 100,180; 20104 -> 201,040). This is the master score itself, in packed BCD, at a x10-per-unit scale (matching the same x10 carry-to-tens-digit relationship already established for this accumulator's connection to ScoreDigit3/4 -- see rom:B406) -- not a separate bonus-life tracker. The reference's suggested identity was a real, useful, testable hypothesis; it just didn't survive the check, and the correction came from this project's own live evidence, not the reference itself.
comments.rom:9DD8: CONFIRMED LIVE: this is what schedules a challenge stage -- the open item flagged in docs/FINDINGS.md as 'what determines a given wave is a challenge wave, still not found'. Runs once per wave, gated on ChallengeCountdown (ram_00BD) reading exactly $60 (the same single-tick gate documented at rom:9D8D). Computes (Wave+2) via repeated SBC #$04 to test whether it's an exact multiple of 4, i.e. whether Wave mod 4 == 2. If so (rom:9DEC), sets ram_0061 = $4F (the challenge-stage-active flag checked at rom:D021) and plays two cue sounds -- this wave IS a challenge stage. If not, and ram_0061 was left set from a challenge stage that just ended (rom:9DFD), clears it, resets ChallengeCountdown to 1, and increments ram_005A (ChallengeValueCycle), wrapping it back to 0 once it reaches 8. LIVE-VERIFIED against run-01.inp (tools/probe-groupvalue.lua, frames 80000-104454): challenge stages fire at exactly wave 26, 30, 34 in that window, matching Wave mod 4 == 2 precisely, with no exceptions. See rom:D097 for what ChallengeValueCycle actually gates and why this directly explains the user's wave-36 point-value hint.
comments.rom:D097: CONFIRMED LIVE, and this is the direct explanation for the user's wave-36 hint ('challenge segments went from 1600 to 1000 points per cleared group'). Runs after every challenge-stage kill; when ChallengeHitCountBin (ram_0063) has just wrapped from 7 back to 0 (i.e. a group of 8 challenge-stage kills has been completed), this stages a score-accumulator add of ram_006D/ram_006E (see rom:93E0 for how that packed-BCD pair gets folded into the real on-screen score) gated on ChallengeValueCycle (ram_005A, incremented once per completed challenge stage and wrapped mod 8 at rom:9DD8): if ChallengeValueCycle >= 4, ram_006E is forced to $60 with ram_006D already $01 -- packed value '0160', which the accumulator's x10-per-carry-unit scaling (documented at rom:93E0/rom:B406) turns into a clean, kill-type-independent +1,600 to the display. If ChallengeValueCycle < 4, ram_006D is set to $01 but ram_006E is left UNTOUCHED here -- it still holds whatever this specific kill's own per-kill point value was written earlier the same frame (rom:D053-D08F, values like $05/$08/$10/$16 -> 50/80/100/160 points) -- so the low-cycle award isn't a clean flat 1,000, it's 1,000 plus that kill's own points, asymmetric with the high-cycle case by design or oversight. Since ChallengeValueCycle cycles 0-7 across 8 consecutive challenge stages (32 waves, one stage per 4 waves per rom:9DD8), stages land in the low half (0-3, ~1,000/group) for waves roughly 2-14 of each 32-wave block and the high half (4-7, exactly 1,600/group) for waves roughly 18-30, then drop straight back to the low half at the next block's first stage. LIVE-VERIFIED against run-01.inp (tools/probe-groupvalue.lua + tools/probe-groupdelta.lua): the wave-30 stage (ChallengeValueCycle=7) awards two clean +1,600 group bonuses; ChallengeValueCycle wraps 7->0 at the end of that stage; the very next stage (wave 34, ChallengeValueCycle=0) awards +1,160 and +1,100 per group (1,000 plus that group's own 8th-kill value, matching the asymmetric-code prediction above) -- and this wave-34 stage is exactly the one that leaves the on-screen wave counter reading 36 once it finishes, matching the user's 'around wave 36' recollection almost exactly. Because ChallengeValueCycle cycles rather than latching permanently, the award should climb back to a flat 1,600/group around wave 50 (the next time the cycle reaches 4) -- not checked live yet, since run-01.inp ends at wave 36.
comments.rom:9065: PARTIAL PROGRESS on the user's tractor-beam hint -- the capture-ATTEMPT mechanism, not yet the formation-kill-vs-diving-kill release branch itself. `rom:sub_903E` runs per-frame on a diving enemy (Y); once it has descended past a fixed depth threshold (ram_1E63,Y >= $78), this sets that enemy's state to a specific attack-pattern value ($03), arms CaptureAttemptTimer (ram_00B4) to $B4 (180), plays two cue sounds, and saves Y into CapturingEnemyIndex (ram_005C) -- this reads as 'this enemy has reached tractor-beam range, start the beam sequence.' `rom:sub_9081` (called once per frame while the timer is armed) decrements it, TWICE per frame once Wave >= 18 (matching the countdown as effectively shorter/harder at higher waves), and once it reaches 0 (`rom:L_909C`) calls `rom:sub_D3D1` (NOT a capture-specific routine -- just the shared sound-channel silence/reset used all over this ROM, a dead end chased and ruled out) and then reassigns the capturing enemy's own state (ram_1F77,Y) as it returns to formation. NOT YET FOUND: anything that reads whether the player's own ship was actually hit by the beam during this window, or sets a 'captured' flag on the player's ship itself -- this pass only confirms the capturing enemy's own side of the sequence. The next concrete lead is CapturingEnemyIndex (ram_005C): read back at `rom:sub_D36C`, itself called from the two CPY #$28 score/spawn branches this project already mapped while solving the wave-36 hint (rom:D01C, rom:D244 -- both awarding 1,000 points and spawning a replacement enemy with state $0B) -- i.e. killing the enemy at the fixed slot $28 goes back and modifies the *original capturing enemy's* own hit-state (ram_1DD3,Y -= 13) via ram_005C, which strongly suggests slot $28 is reserved specifically for a captured/escorted entity tied back to whichever enemy captured it -- but the exact mechanics of that link, and where the hostile-vs-escort behavioral split the user described actually lives, are still unresolved. UPDATE, directly screenshot-verified (tools/probe-capture2.lua, -nothrottle, per standing project practice for a long recording): the user confirmed live that capture events happened 'a few times early on in the run', so this was tapped wide -- every write to CaptureAttemptTimer and CapturingEnemyIndex across frames 0-40000 (waves 1-5), not just the two rare score/spawn-flag events found while solving the wave-36 hint. Found FIVE capture-arm events (not two), reusing two formation slots (CapturingEnemyIndex=$1A twice, $11 twice, $23 once). Screenshotted the aftermath of every one: ALL FIVE show the actual on-screen 'FIGHTER CAPTURED' text and tractor-beam graphic (a striped triangle from the diving boss down to the player), roughly 60 frames (1 second) after the depth-threshold arm -- well inside the 180-frame countdown this comment already describes, confirming there's a separate, still-unfound beam/player collision check that fires independently of (and faster than) the countdown's own natural expiry. Also confirmed live: getting captured costs a life exactly like dying (a 'READY' respawn prompt follows immediately, and the ship-icon lives count drops by one) -- this ROM's tractor beam is not survivable without either evading it or destroying the diver before the beam connects. Sequencing the frame numbers against the game's own resets (ram_005C also gets zeroed at rom:B145 on at least 3 apparent game-over/restart events in this same window) made the frame-23569 capture (wave 1) and the already-mapped Y==0x28 kill at frame 26758 (wave 2, +1,000 points, rom:D01C) look like the same continuity, and this comment previously guessed from that alone that the 1,000-point/spawn-flag-$0B outcome was the 'released as hostile' case from the user's hint. RETRACTED: the user then supplied further ground truth (dual-fighter for most of a 37-wave run, one hit reverting it to single) that led to directly finding DualFighterFlag (ram_1E11, see rom:92B3) and empirically checking its two real formation events against every write in the surrounding window -- neither lines up with a $0B/CPY #$28 event. The formation-vs-diving kill distinction from the user's original hint is NOT the CPY #$28-vs-sub_D29F split this project guessed here; see rom:92B3 for what's actually confirmed instead (the rescue-completion and hit-reversion mechanics), and for what's still genuinely open (the exact trigger that arms the returning-captive sequence in the first place).
comments.rom:B01D: RESOLVED (closes the 'whether CHARBASE gets set anywhere in this ROM at all' item from docs/FINDINGS.md). This is CHARBASE's only write in the whole ROM (confirmed: no gaps exist per disasm.py --gaps, and no second writer turns up in a full-file grep), and it IS a deliberate one -- not just incidentally caught by the generic zero-page sweep a few instructions earlier (rom:B00F's loop only covers $0040-$00FF; CHARBASE at $0034 sits below that range and is zeroed by this explicit STA, alongside a short list of other specific addresses named individually: ram_277F, ram_2783-2785, ram_1D20-1D21). Set once at boot to 0 and never touched again for the rest of execution. Reads as this ROM using Maria's direct (non-CHARBASE-relative) display-list addressing throughout, where CHARBASE genuinely doesn't matter -- not an oversight or a mystery, just a register this ROM doesn't use.
comments.rom:92B3: CONFIRMED LIVE, and this closes most of the user's tractor-beam hint (see rom:9065 for the capture-attempt side; this is the release/rescue side). DualFighterFlag (ram_1E11, newly named) is the player's escort-attached state -- set here to 5 as the tail end of a multi-stage 'returning captive' animation inside rom:sub_9250 (called unconditionally every frame from the main loop, gated internally on ram_1E43 reaching $50, then ram_1E8B reaching $AB, then PlayerX (ram_1E5A, newly named) reading exactly $49 -- the captive ship's own return flight catching up to the player's position). LIVE-VERIFIED via cluster analysis across four screenshot-confirmed frames (single at wave 5 and wave 28, dual at wave 12 and wave 26) and via a direct PC-tagged write-tap: BOTH real occurrences of this write in the first 55,000 frames (frame 13,953 and frame 37,713) fire from this exact instruction. The first is short-lived (reverts by frame 14,964, ~17 seconds later); the second is the long-lived one that persists from wave 5 through wave 26 -- genuinely 'most of the run' the way the user described, once the early false-start games (see rom:9065's capture-attempt comment) settle into the long sustained session. RETRACTS a specific circumstantial guess made in an earlier pass of this same file: linking the CPY #$28/spawn-flag-$0B path (rom:D01C) to 'released as hostile' turned out to be unconfirmed by direct timing -- neither of the two real DualFighterFlag-forming events lines up with a $0B write in the same window. UPDATE: what triggers the *start* of the returning-captive sequence is now found too, from a second recording the user made specifically to catch it (run-02.inp) -- see rom:90DE. It is NOT a kill event at all: see rom:90DE for the full mechanism, CORRECTED after an initial pass wrongly concluded the capture itself was being prevented (the user caught this directly: a real capture, with its usual text and life cost, was sitting in the very screenshots that pass had taken but not actually looked at). What's actually true: the capture always runs its full course; a separate proximity check during a specific window of that same sequence determines whether the captured ship gets queued to automatically merge with the next spawned ship, rather than being lost for good. Still genuinely open: whether a kill-based rescue path (shoot the diving captor) *also* exists in this ROM alongside the proximity-based one -- no evidence for one has turned up, but that's weaker now that the proximity mechanism has needed one real correction already. What's settled: getting hit while DualFighterFlag is set does NOT cost a life -- rom:sub_D1D3 (reached from the player-collision code at rom:sub_D0C7) clears it back to 0 instead of running the normal death path, matching the user's 'the first hit only brings it back to a single fighter' exactly.
comments.rom:90DE: CORRECTED (the user caught this directly: 'a life was lost and a fighter capture shown in the shots you were looking at' -- a real self-check failure, not a subtle one: the first pass only viewed a handful of the screenshots it had already taken and skipped right over the ones showing the capture text, then wrote up 'no capture happens' from that gap). RETRACTED: sub_90DE does NOT prevent a capture, and this ROM's tractor beam is not evadable by repositioning. Re-verified frame-by-frame against run-02.inp with a direct write-tap on ram_0089 plus PlayerX/CaptureOriginX/CaptureAttemptTimer sampled every 10 frames (tools/probe-run02verify.lua) and a full screenshot sweep at 5-frame resolution across the whole capture window (tools/probe-run02recheck.lua, this time actually viewed in full): the capture runs its complete, ordinary course --CaptureAttemptTimer decrements 180->0 with no interruption, 'FIGHTER CAPTURED' is on screen for roughly 80 frames (first visible ~frame 3670, gone by ~3800), the ship-icon lives count drops from 2 to 1, and a 'READY' respawn prompt follows (~frame 3900) -- exactly like every capture in run-01.inp. What sub_90DE actually does: it runs during a specific mid-countdown band of CaptureAttemptTimer ($3C-$78) and checks whether PlayerX is still within 12 pixels of CaptureOriginX (ram_64, the position saved at the instant of arming, rom:sub_903E) -- in this recording the player barely moved during the (likely input-locked) capture animation, so the check passed almost immediately (arming ram_0089 at frame 3,629, well inside the predicted 3,628-3,688 window, confirmed by a direct write-tap). That flag sits pending -- consumed only once the new ship is up and controllable again (ram_0089 cleared at frame 3,876 by rom:sub_8B53, right around when PlayerX starts changing again, i.e. the respawned ship moving under real input) -- and queues the returning-captive animation that completes at rom:92B3 (DualFighterFlag set at frame 5,007 in this recording). The corrected picture: getting captured still costs a life and plays out in full, exactly as it always did -- but if the ship stayed near the capture point during a specific window of that same sequence, the captured ship is queued to automatically merge with the very next spawned ship as an escort, rather than being lost for good or turning hostile. Genuinely still open: whether this position check is close to automatic in practice (since the captured ship may not be player-movable during the beam sequence at all, making the 12-pixel window easy to satisfy passively) or whether it can meaningfully fail -- run-01.inp had five confirmed captures but only two real DualFighterFlag-forming events in the same recording, so it evidently doesn't always succeed; what differs between the two recordings' cases hasn't been checked. FURTHER UPDATE, from the user watching this exact recording and pointing at the specific kill: 'the specific foe is killed when the score turns 4500->4900, spins for a couple of seconds' -- and this is directly confirmed. That kill (frame 4,609, going through the same sub_CFEA/sub_CFEF collision-resolution path already mapped for the wave-36 hint, landing on the ordinary +400 default case, not the CPY #$28 branch) sits right where ram_1E43/ram_1E8B (tracked live via tools/probe-run02kill2.lua, sampled every 5 frames) FREEZE -- both hold constant from frame ~4,610 to ~4,870 -- and a tight consecutive-frame screenshot check during that freeze shows a small sprite visibly changing shape/orientation frame to frame at the kill site: a real spin, not a static object. Once the freeze ends (~4,870), ram_1E43 climbs cleanly to $50 and ram_1E8B to $AB, completing at frame 5,007 -- matching 'a couple of seconds' for the visible spin-and-return well. This means the EARLIER framing in this comment ('the proximity check at frame 3,629 is what leads to the merge') is likely incomplete or wrong: that arm event happens far too early (1,378 frames before completion) to explain a 'couple of seconds' spin tied to a specific kill 1,040 frames later. The more likely shape: something (possibly this same proximity check) arms a WATCHER early, but the actual captive can't begin its own tracked return until whatever is carrying it is destroyed -- plausibly gated on whether the enemy at CapturingEnemyIndex (ram_005C) is still alive, though this specific linkage has NOT been confirmed at the instruction level (no PC has been identified that reads CapturingEnemyIndex and gates ram_1E43/ram_1E8B's progression on it). SOLVED -- see rom:9250 for the full mechanism, found without consulting the private reference. ram_1E43/ram_1E8B were never shared scratch bytes touched by an unrelated enemy's animation -- that reading (from rom:sub_915D also writing them) was itself off by one level of indirection: they are ram_1E1B[$28]/ram_1E63[$28] (slot $28's own X/Y position, hit via a hardcoded address instead of Y-indexed addressing), and sub_915D firing was ALSO slot $28's own code, just a different phase of its own state machine (driven by the same ram_1F9F = ram_1F77[$28] byte), not a different enemy at all. The real gate: rom:sub_9250, dispatched on ram_1F9F, holds in a waiting state (value 8) until ram_0088 (a repeating current-dive-group-remaining counter, confirmed cycling 0-8-0 throughout ordinary play) reaches zero -- and at the user-identified kill (frame 4,609) it does, in the same instant. FURTHER CONFIRMED VISUALLY, per the user's direct instruction to check right before the kill: 'the captured fighter and the boss fly in formation.' Screenshotted every 20 frames from the moment the new ship respawns (frame 3,900, 'READY' still on screen) through the kill (frame 4,609) and found the SAME two-sprite pair (a white moth-shaped enemy directly paired with a smaller blue enemy, always adjacent, moving together) visible continuously across that entire ~700-frame span -- present at frame 3,900 right as the new ship spawns, still paired at frames 4,100/4,300/4,400/4,460, and diving toward the player still paired at frame 4,600, nine frames before the kill. This is strong, direct visual confirmation of the user's original hint's basic shape (a boss carries a captured fighter with it, visibly, until something happens to release it). CORRECTED identification, per the user directly comparing a zoomed screenshot against the player's own ship visible in the same frame: the sprite originally guessed to be 'the boss' (the upper one, white with a red/pink center) is shaped almost identically to the player's own ship rendered lower in the same screenshot -- it is much more likely the CAPTURED PLAYER FIGHTER, reusing the player's own graphics, with the lower BLUE sprite (a different, shield-like shape) being the actual capturing enemy/boss -- the reverse of this project's first guess. Geometry matches too: the player-shaped sprite sits above, the enemy below, consistent with a captured ship riding attached to its captor. The user also flagged the methodological point directly: ordinary formation enemies fly paired only during the wave's own pre-formation flight-in choreography, not persistently mid-wave -- so a tight, sustained pairing like this one, well after formation is established, is itself a meaningful signal distinguishing it from ordinary group movement, not just an incidental coincidence. The exact code linkage from 'this enemy is destroyed' to 'the freeze at rom:9250 ends' (see above) is still not pinned down at the instruction level despite this strong visual support. Also confirmed by the user: real flagships in this game can carry up to two escorts flying in formation below them (per this project's own manual summary at the top of docs/FINDINGS.md), which could have been an alternative explanation for the paired blue sprite -- ruled out directly: no escorts are present on this particular flagship in run-02.inp, so the paired sprite is not one of the normal two-escort formation and the captured-player-fighter identification above stands.
comments.rom:8FAC: A real, structurally-confirmed piece of the tractor-beam mechanism, found while chasing what gates the kill-triggered spin-and-return (see rom:90DE for the full story). This routine runs when processing the special slot $28 entity -- the captured-player-fighter visual, per the user's corrected identification at rom:90DE -- and checks whether the enemy at CapturingEnemyIndex (ram_005C) is still alive (ram_1DD3,X nonzero). If it is, nothing changes. If it's dead, this searches a FIXED list of four formation slots -- $06, $11, $1A, $23 -- via rom:sub_8FD4, looking for the first one still alive, and REASSIGNS CapturingEnemyIndex to that slot if found (rom:8FDE). These four slots line up with real capture-arm data: two of the five capture events found live in run-01.inp used CapturingEnemyIndex values $1A and $11 -- both members of this exact fixed set -- strongly suggesting these are the ROM's four fixed 'flagship' formation positions (the only slots eligible to carry a tractor beam and a captive). The companion routine (rom:sub_8FF6 onward) uses whichever index this resolves to (falling back to a default per-slot table, dat_937D, if NO candidate among the five is alive) to read a target position each frame and steer slot $28's own movement toward it -- this is the code making the captured-fighter sprite visually track and follow a living boss, directly explaining the ~700-frame formation-flying the user pointed out and this project screenshotted (see rom:90DE). CONFIRMED, see rom:9250: ram_1E43/ram_1E8B are ram_1E1B[$28]/ram_1E63[$28] -- slot $28's own position, not shared scratch touched by a different enemy as this comment first guessed. The actual gate on the captive's return is ram_0088 (a repeating dive-group-remaining counter) reaching zero, checked by rom:sub_9250's own state-8 wait; the five-slot fallback list here explains the formation-tracking visual, and rom:9250 explains the release timing.
comments.rom:9250: SOLVES the last open piece of the tractor-beam investigation -- found without consulting the private reference source, using the same PC-tagged write-tap technique this project has used throughout. This is the master dispatcher for slot $28 (the captured-fighter entity, see rom:90DE and rom:8FAC), gated on its own state byte ram_1F9F (= ram_1F77+$28, the same per-enemy state array used everywhere else in this ROM, just hit via a hardcoded address here instead of Y-indexed addressing -- the same pattern explains ram_1E43/ram_1E8B below, which are ram_1E1B[$28]/ram_1E63[$28], the captive's own X/Y position, confirmed by write-tap hits at rom:9B3B/rom:9B69 where STA ram_1E63,Y/STA ram_1E1B,Y fire with Y=$28). State 9 runs the already-known climb-to-completion logic (L_9273: increment/decrement ram_1E43 toward $50, then ram_1E8B toward $AB, then require PlayerX==$49, completing at rom:92B3). State 8 is a WAITING state: it requires ram_0088 to be zero (and a secondary counter, ram_1ED3, to also be zero) before advancing to state 9 -- otherwise it just increments ram_1ED3 and returns, frame after frame, doing nothing else. ram_0088 is a repeating enemy counter -- confirmed live cycling 0->8 (armed via rom:97F9, an enemy entering its diving pass) then 8->0 (decremented on each kill within that pass, via several different kill-dispatch addresses depending on enemy type) roughly every 350-400 frames throughout ordinary play in run-02.inp, independent of the capture story -- it tracks how many members of the CURRENT active dive group are still alive, not anything capture-specific on its own. LIVE-CONFIRMED: at the user-identified kill (frame 4,609, score 4500->4900), ram_0088 goes from 1 to 0 in the same instant (write-tap on rom:CFFC). The state-8-to-9 transition itself fires later, at frame 4,864 (rom:926A) -- a ~255-frame gap not fully explained (plausibly ram_1ED3 needing its own reset from a prior waiting cycle before this specific check can pass; not traced further) -- but the causal chain is now solid: the kill the user pointed to was the one that emptied the captor's own dive group, which is what state 8 was actually waiting on the whole time. The mechanism is very slightly more general than 'kill the boss': it's 'clear the boss's entire dive group', and in this recording the boss happened to be the last member of that group killed -- which is why killing it specifically was what the user (correctly) identified as the trigger.

blocks.name: dat_FF76
blocks.note: CONFIRMED by inspection, no xrefs anywhere in traced code (checked): the first 10 bytes decode as ASCII 'GCC(c)1984' -- General Computer Corporation's own copyright/signature string, same exact pattern (identical size: 138 bytes, same relative position right after a bare JMP entry point) found in the Dig Dug (7800) project's own tail region -- independently re-confirmed here by reading this ROM's own bytes, not assumed from that project. Followed by ~122 bytes with no discernible structure (not ASCII, no repeating pattern, no xrefs) -- almost certainly unused filler/padding.
